interpretations: Per-equipment average is taken over all `scanenvironment` rows for that `equipref`, ignoring NULL `humepct`. "All-equipment average" is the unweighted mean of the per-equipment averages. Equipment with no non-null readings is excluded from that mean. Keep equipment with average strictly above it. Output the equipment reference, its average humidity, its excess over the all-equipment average, and its difference from the mean of the kept equipment's averages. Sort by that last difference, descending, NULLs last. Return 10 rows, with ties at 10th place broken arbitrarily
Same as 1, but the "all-equipment average" is the row-weighted mean of all non-null `humepct` readings. It is not the mean of the per-equipment averages
Same as 1, but equipment with no non-null readings counts as an equipment with a NULL average. It stays in the equipment list and is dropped only by the "above average" filter
Same as 1, but the equipment list comes from the `equipment` table (`equipregistry`), so equipment with no environment rows is included with a NULL average
"Difference from the mean of just the kept equipment" means the average humidity minus the mean of the kept equipment's averages. This is signed, so it can be negative
The same difference taken as an absolute value, so the sort is by distance from the kept-group mean
"Exceeds the all-equipment average" is read as the plain difference (average − overall average). It is always positive after filtering
"Exceeds" is read as a percentage or ratio over the overall average, not an absolute difference

"Return nothing if either reference average is missing" means that if the overall average or the kept-group average is NULL, the query returns zero rows. This is the same as 1 in effect, since a kept row implies both averages exist
"Return nothing" is read as returning one row of NULLs instead of an empty result
"Above" is read as greater than or equal to the overall average, so equipment exactly at the average is kept

Sort is by the difference from the kept-group mean, descending. Since the kept mean is a constant, this is the same as sorting by average humidity descending. Ties are broken arbitrarily, with no secondary key
The tie rule is read as a strict `LIMIT 10` with an arbitrary tie-break. Alternatively, it could be read as a deterministic tie-break such as `equipref` ascending
Fewer than 10 equipment qualify. Return all of them, not exactly 10 rows. Alternatively, pad the result to 10 rows with NULLs
Equipment is grouped by `scanenvironment.equipref` as a raw string. Alternatively, it is grouped after trimming or normalizing case
Averages are rounded to some number of decimal places before comparing or displaying. Alternatively, they are left at full precision
Humidity values outside 0–100 are excluded as invalid. Alternatively, all non-null values are included as they are
Missing interpretations:

The mean humidity of just the kept equipment is the row-weighted mean of all non-null `humepct` readings belonging to the kept equipment, not the unweighted mean of their per-equipment averages. The all-equipment average stays the mean of per-equipment averages, as in interpretation

Both reference averages are row-weighted: the all-equipment average is the mean of all non-null readings, and the kept-group mean is the mean of the kept equipment's readings. This differs from interpretation 2, where only the all-equipment average is weighted
queries:
WITH per AS (
  SELECT equipref, AVG(humepct) AS avg_hum
  FROM scanenvironment
  GROUP BY equipref
  HAVING COUNT(humepct) > 0
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_hum) AS all_avg FROM per
),
kept AS (
  SELECT p.equipref, p.avg_hum, p.avg_hum - o.all_avg AS excess
  FROM per p, overall o
  WHERE p.avg_hum > o.all_avg
)
SELECT equipref,
       avg_hum AS average_humidity,
       excess AS excess_over_all_average,
       avg_hum - (SELECT AVG(avg_hum) FROM kept) AS diff_from_kept_mean
FROM kept
ORDER BY diff_from_kept_mean DESC
LIMIT 10;
SELECT equipref
FROM scanenvironment
WHERE humepct IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY equipref
HAVING AVG(humepct) > (SELECT AVG(humepct) FROM scanenvironment WHERE humepct IS NOT NULL);
SELECT e.equipregistry
FROM equipment e
LEFT JOIN scanenvironment s ON s.equipref = e.equipregistry
GROUP BY e.equipregistry
HAVING AVG(s.ambictemp) > (SELECT AVG(ambictemp) FROM scanenvironment);
SELECT e.equipregistry, AVG(se.ambictemp) AS avg_ambictemp
FROM equipment e
LEFT JOIN scanenvironment se ON se.equipref = e.equipregistry
GROUP BY e.equipregistry;
WITH eq_avg AS (
  SELECT equipref, AVG(humepct) AS avg_humidity
  FROM scanenvironment
  GROUP BY equipref
)
SELECT equipref, avg_humidity, avg_humidity - (SELECT AVG(avg_humidity) FROM eq_avg) AS diff_from_mean
FROM eq_avg;
